paper_title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Real-world image search queries are multimodal and compositional: ``find this shirt in pink'' specifies an entity to retain, an attribute to modify, and context to ignore. Yet existing re-rankers either compress such multifaceted relevance into an opaque embedding or rely on free-form chain-of-thought that easily omits or hallucinates fine-grained constraints. Drawing on rubric- and checklist-based evaluation from NLP, we recast multimodal image re-ranking as a semantic constraint satisfaction problem and propose EviRank, which parses any query - text-only, image-only, or composed - into a unified evidence package: typed criteria across six semantic slots (e.g., entities, attributes, relations), each labelled required, forbidden, or ignorable. Re-ranking then reduces to evidence-conditioned verification, combining deterministic rubric scoring and evidence-grounded listwise comparison in a single training-free procedure. The explicit evidence can further serve as structured supervision for optionally distilling a lightweight student. Across five benchmarks spanning text-to-image, image-to-image, and composed image retrieval, EviRank achieves state-of-the-art performance, and the distilled student preserves over 90% of the teacher's capability at substantially lower cost.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Real-world image search queries are rarely singlefaceted. user asking find this shirt in pink is implicitly specifying multiple semantic constraints Work done during an internship at Tencent. *Corresponding author. 1 at once: the system must retain the entity shirt together with its visual identity (cut, pattern, fit), modify specific attribute (color pink), and ignore incidental factors such as background or lighting in the reference image (Xing et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2025a; Tian et al., 2025). Such queries naturally combine information from multiple modalities text, image, or bothand constrain the target along several semantic dimensions, such as entities, attributes, actions, relations, and discriminative details. Whether the query is purely textual, purely visual, or mixture of the two, the underlying problem is the same: deciding whether each candidate image satisfies the set of fine-grained semantic constraints that the query imposes. Existing multimodal re-rankers, however, do not explicitly model these constraints. Representationcentric approachesranging from classical dualencoder embeddings (Frome et al., 2013) to recent MLLM-based scorers (Liu et al., 2025c; Huynh et al., 2025; Sun et al., 2025b)collapse all semantic dimensions of query into single dense vector. Such an opaque representation cannot tell which evidence should be preserved, modified, or ignored, and offers no handle on fine-grained constraint violations. Reasoning-centric approaches (Sun et al., 2025a; Wu et al., 2025) instead ask an MLLM to reason about relevance in free-form chain-ofthought (CoT). While more expressive, this freeform reasoning remains unstructured natural language, and exhibits three concrete failure modes. First, it omits implicit constraints: when user says find this shirt in pink, CoT trace typically discusses the color change while silently dropping the preserve the original cut and pattern constraint. Second, it hallucinates evidence, attributing Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent visual properties the model has not actually verified. Third, its semantic coverage is inconsistent across queries, so completeness and verifiability of the relevance judgement cannot be guaranteed without formal structure specifying which dimensions must be examined. These failure modes share common root: multimodal image re-ranking is fundamentally semantic constraint satisfaction problem, not generic similarity-matching problem, and methods that do not represent constraints explicitly cannot systematically verify them. We therefore propose to represent multimodal relevance as structured Evidence Frame. Instead of free-form reasoning, we first parse the query into typed evidence statementsREQUIRED, FORBIDDEN, and IGNORABLEorganized along six semantic slots (entities, attributes, actions, relations, scene, and key details; full definitions in Section 3.1). The three labels mirror well-studied semantic relations (entailment, contradiction, and invariance, respectively; Section 3.1). Since the Evidence Frame is modality-agnostic, text-only, image-only and composed queries share single evidence interface. Re-ranking then reduces to verifying which constraints each candidate satisfies or violatesa slot-wise, language-grounded judgement that is transparent and deterministically aggregable. Building on this representation, EviRank reranks top-K candidates in two stagesevidence mining and evidence verificationboth trainingfree. The same slot-wise satisfaction scores and hard-pair distinctions also serve as naturally decomposable supervision for distilling lightweight student re-ranker. Our core contributions are: new formulation. We formulate multimodal image re-ranking as evidence-conditioned semantic verification, where text-only, image-only and composed queries are converted into shared Evidence Frame of typed relevance criteria (required / forbidden / ignorable, instantiated as entailment / contradiction / invariance). Evidence mining and evidence verification. We design training-free, evidence-conditioned re-ranking procedure that mines slot-wise required, forbidden, and ignorable evidence, and verifies it through deterministic rubric grounded in the same evidence. Evidence as supervision. We show that the structured evidence and its slot-wise verification signals form naturally decomposable supervision source, which can be distilled into compact student re-ranker. Experiments. State-of-the-art results across five benchmarks, with analysis showing the structured evidence is robust, interpretable, and contributes beyond free-form augmentation.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Implicit Relevance Representations for Multimodal Retrieval. first family encodes queries and candidate images into joint embedding space and ranks by similarity (Frome et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2024; Levy et al., 2024; Bai et al., 2024); recent MLLM-based re-rankers continue this paradigm by distilling multimodal capability into improved embeddings or learned scoring heads (Liu et al., 2025c; Huynh et al., 2025; Sun et al., 2025b; Lin et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2024), while complementary line reformulates retrieval as document-identifier generation (Tay et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022; Li et al., 2024). All of them represent relevance implicitlya scalar similarity, an opaque embedding, or learned ID distribution and cannot tell which semantic dimensions of query candidate satisfies or violates. Our work is orthogonal: we operate on top of any such retriever and replace its implicit score with explicit, slot-wise evidence verification. Free-form Reasoning for Image Re-ranking. second family augments MLLM-based re-ranking with CoT reasoning (Sun et al., 2025a; Wu et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2025b; Luo et al., 2025). More expressive than single similarity score, the reasoning trace nonetheless remains unstructured natural language and exhibits the omission, hallucination, and inconsistent-coverage failures discussed in Section 1. EviRank instead asks the teacher for typed Evidence Frame (required / forbidden / ignorable over six semantic slots) that can be verified, aggregated, and distilled. Novelty delineation. Our claim is representational rather than about what MLLMs can reason about. ImageScope decomposes query into multi-granularity hierarchy, CoTRR into five reasoning components and CoTMR into predefined verification subtasks, yet in all three the intermediate product is free-form text whose fields are neither typed nor guaranteed to recur across queries. Structured Criteria for Semantic Verification. The NLP community has increasingly turned to structured rubricand checklist-based evaluation, where complex semantic judgements are decomposed into independently checkable criteria (Liu et al., 2023; Cook et al., 2024; Lee et al., 2025; Wei et al., 2025), and rubric criteria are further used as RL reward signals (Zhou et al., 2025; Arora et al., 2025). closely related line decomposes complex claims into verifiable sub-units for fact checking and faithfulness evaluation (Thorne et al., 2018; Min et al., 2023; Golovneva et al., 2023), while further line makes the intermediate structure itself explicit and inspectableas provenance-constrained evidence ledger, as reasoning paths or relational digraphs over graph (Du et al., 2026, 2025; Zhang et al., 2026, 2023), or as structure shared between neural reasoner and an LLM (Liu et al., 2025a). EviRank imports the same decompose-then-verify principle into multimodal image re-ranking: multimodal query becomes typed evidence statements over six semantic slots, and relevance is established by slot-wise, languagegrounded verification rather than by opaque similarity or free-form CoT.

sections.title: 3 Method
sections.content: We present EviRank (Figure 1), which recasts multimodal image re-ranking as semantic constraint satisfaction: query is parsed into unified package of structured evidence criteria, and candidates are re-ranked by checking which criteria they satisfy or violate. Section 3.1 defines the setting and evidence representation; Sections 3.2 and 3.3 describe evidence mining and evidence-conditioned verification and re-ranking; and Section 3.4 shows how the same evidence serves as decomposable supervision for distilling lightweight re-ranker. 3.1 Setting and Evidence Representation Setting. We consider multimodal image reranking. query may consist of text, an image, or bothwithout loss of generality, we write = (t, Iref) where either component may be empty. Given and top-K candidate set CK = {c1, . . . , cK} produced by any off-the-shelf retriever, the goal of re-ranking is to output permutation π over CK that better reflects semantic relevance. From queries to evidence. Our central observation is that, regardless of how is expressed, it implicitly defines set of semantic constraints on the target image: some elements must be present, others must not, and many are simply irrelevant. We therefore represent relevance not by similarity score, but by typed evidence package E(q) = (cid:0)g, {(Rs, Fs, Is)}sS (cid:1), (1) where is concise global summary of the query intent and is lightweight default schema of six semantic slots, (cid:40) = ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTES, ACTIONS, RELATIONS, SCENE, KEYDETAILS (cid:41) . Slots are allowed to remain empty when the query does not express the corresponding factor (e.g., still-life caption typically populates ENTITIES and ATTRIBUTES but leaves ACTIONS and RELATIONS empty), and the schema can be extended with additional slots for specialized domains without changing the verification procedure. Each slot contributes three lists of short, checkable sentences: required constraints Rs that must hold, forbidden constraints Fs that must not hold, and ignorable constraints Is that should not influence the decision (Appendix draws an analogy between this typing and classical SQL constraints). 3 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent Figure 1: Overview of EviRank. multimodal query (text-only, image-only, or composed) and top-K candidates from any retriever are first parsed by an MLLM teacher into structured Evidence Frame of typed required / forbidden / ignorable statements over six semantic slots. Candidates are then re-ranked by evidence-conditioned verification (deterministic rubric + MLLM listwise refinement). The same evidence yields structured supervision bundle that is distilled into lightweight student; at inference the student consumes only the raw query and candidate image. Unifying heterogeneous query forms. key property of this representation is that it is modalityagnostic: although users may issue queries in very different forms, the resulting evidence package always lives in the same schema. purely textual query becomes evidence whose required slots reflect what the user verbalizes and whose ignorable slots absorb under-specified context. purely visual query is first captioned and then converted to evidence in which the reference images salient content becomes the required constraints. composed query (image + modification text) is mapped to evidence by treating the reference image as source of preserved required constraints (e.g., shirt cut and pattern) and the modification text as source of updated required constraints together with newly induced forbidden constraints (e.g., original color pink, so the shirt is of the original color becomes forbidden). After this normalization, all subsequent stages of EviRank operate on the same evidence schema, so heterogeneous query forms can be handled through shared evidence-verification interface rather than paradigm-specific re-ranking pipelines. 3.2 Query-to-Evidence Mining Building the evidence package E(q) proceeds in two training-free steps performed by single multimodal model (referred to as the MLLM teacher throughout this paper). Query normalization. Different query forms expose different amounts of information. Text queries are explicit but often under-specified; image queries are visually rich but lexically unanchored; composed queries entangle both. We therefore first normalize into textual representation that exposes its semantic content in uniform way. For text queries, we verbalize into that makes implicit visual details (identity, scene, salient attributes) explicit, while preserving the original intent. For image queries, we generate concise caption together with key objects. For composed queries, we combine the reference caption with the modification text and explicitly mark which aspects should be preserved versus modified. This step is training-free; it serves purely as semantic enrichment for downstream evidence extraction, not as an additional retrieval pass. Evidence extraction. Given the normalized query, the MLLM emits the full evidence package E(q) in single structured pass. For each slot S, the model produces 24 short affirmative sentences for each of Rs, Fs, and Is. Critically, even forbidden constraints are written as positive statements that describe what an incorrect match would look like (e.g., the shirt is red), so that every constraint can be compared to candidate 4 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent by the same matching operator and yields signconsistent scores during verification. Ignorable constraints explicitly enumerate non-discriminative variations (e.g., minor shade shifts, background lighting) that should be tolerated rather than penalized. The full prompts used for query normalization and evidence extraction are in Appendix H. The six slots cover the principal semantic axes of multimodal queries (entities, attributes, actions, relations, scene, key details) and are empirically near-orthogonal (mean pairwise SBERT similarity 0.18; full slot-semantics analysis in Appendix L); the schema is default rather than hard requirement (cf. Evidence-grounded listwise refinement. The rubric is stable and interpretable but evaluates candidates independently and therefore cannot easily resolve close calls between visually similar candidates. We address this with an evidence-grounded listwise step. The teacher is shown the query, the global intent together with the required and forbidden constraints of E(q), and the candidates jointly, and is asked to return permutation in which required constraints raise rank when clearly satisfied and forbidden constraints heavily penalize salient mismatches. Ignorable constraints are not exposed to the listwise prompt; they act as an invariance mask inside the deterministic rubric only, keeping the prompt compact and avoiding asking the teacher to reason over non-discriminative details. In practice, we sort candidates by Srub and invoke the teacher only to verify and locally reorder the top-M (M =5 by default), which substantially reduces cost while preserving accuracy. Beyond the final ranking, the listwise step naturally produces JSON-formatted artifact containing percandidate relevance scores, self-assessed confidence, and short list of hard pairs (closest competitors with brief distinguishing reasons). sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: EviRank shows that multimodal image re-ranking is, at its core, language-grounded semantic verification: turning query into typed required / forbidden / ignorable constraints lets re-ranker reason about which dimensions matter and how candidate satisfies them, instead of committing the decision to an opaque similarity score or an unstructured chain-of-thought. Three findings recur across our five benchmarks: rubric scoring and listwise comparison are complementary; forbidden constraints, often overlooked in retrieval design, are critical for fine-grained discrimination; and structured evidence is robust across teachers, prompts and decoding randomness. The same formulation generalizes to NLP judgement tasks decomposable into typed atomic units, and distils into compact student retaining over 90% of the teachers capability.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Our evaluation uses widely adopted public image retrieval benchmarks in English, which are standard for the community but do not capture every deployment condition that real-world systems encounter (e.g., multilingual queries, evolving content distributions, or domain-specific corpora outside common benchmark coverage). We also focus on still-image retrieval; extending the framework to Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent video, 3D or audiovisual content is an interesting direction. Finally, we report retrieval metrics on offline benchmarks; large-scale human-facing user studies in production search are left as natural next step. sections.title: Package
sections.content: This appendix complements Section 3.3 with the batching strategy used for evidence-grounded listwise refinement, and the full schema of the byproduct supervision bundle that is later reused in distillation (Section 3.4). Divide-and-merge batching. When the candidate pool is large (K > 8), single listwise call becomes prompt-length-bound and unstable. We therefore partition the candidates into groups of size (default B=5), rank each group independently conditioned on the same evidence package E(q), and iteratively merge the resulting sub-lists by pairwise listwise re-ranking. Writing = K/B for the number of groups, the procedure issues group calls plus 1 pairwise merge calls, i.e. 2n 1 = O(K/B) MLLM calls in total. Because all merges at the same level of the binary merge tree are independent, they can be issued concurrently, so the sequential depthand hence wall-clock latency under parallel clientis 1 + log2 rounds. The logarithmic factor therefore describes latency, not total call count. Rich signal package. single listwise call produces, in addition to the permutation π = (π1, . . . , πK), the following structured artifact for each querycandidate list: Absolute relevance scores {ri}K i=1 on bounded scale (0100), enabling calibrated comparisons across queries. self-assessed confidence [0, 1] reflecting how decisively the candidates can be ordered under the current evidence. set of hard pairs = {(i, j)} consisting of the closest competitors, each accompanied by short distinguishing reason that references specific constraints in E(q). Optional slot-wise signals: per-slot binary indicators ys,i = 1[Matchs(ci) > θ] and the corresponding rates from the deterministic rubric. All of these signals share fixed JSON schema, are produced by the same evidence-conditioned pipeline, and are consumed verbatim by the distillation stageno additional supervision labelling is required.

sections.title: B Additional Distillation Details
sections.content: The three component objectives and the confidenceweighted total loss are defined in Section 3.4 (Eq. 4). This appendix records the motivation behind each term and the implementation details omitted there. Why teacher scores are standardized. The teacher reports absolute relevance on bounded 0100 scale, but its effective dynamic range varies with query difficulty: an unambiguous query may yield {95, 90, 20, . . .} while hard one yields {62, 60, 58, . . .}. Per-query standardization by µr, σr removes this query-level scale, so Lscore transfers the shape of the teachers preference distribution rather than its absolute calibration. Student scores are not standardizedthey are already produced by trainable headand both sides share the single temperature τ . The constant ϵ = 108 only guards against degenerate lists in which all teacher scores coincide. Why hard pairs are weighted by the inverse score gap. Hard pairs are exactly the comparisons that bi-encoder gets wrong, and their difficulty is not uniform: pair separated by one point of teacher score is far more informative than one separated by thirty. The weight wij therefore grows as the gap ri rj shrinks, concentrating gradient mass on the closest competitors, while the margin δ prevents the loss from being driven to zero by an arbitrarily large score difference. The pair set is taken verbatim from the teachers listwise output; no additional mining is performed. Slot auxiliary head. The slot head is small linear projection on top of the students pooled query candidate representation, producing one logit per slot S, and is supervised only by the teachers binary indicators ys,i = 1[Matchs(ci) > θ]. It is used as regularizer that forces the shared representation to encode constraint-level evidence rather than single scalar preference; the head is dropped after training, so deployed inference cost is identical to plain scoring student. When slot-wise labels are missing for query, Lslot is skipped for that query rather than filled with pseudo-labels. Hyperparameters and stability. We use τ =2.0, δ=0.5, λ=0.5 and η=0.3, selected on the validation split; the full configuration is listed in Table 11 in Appendix D. The confidence weight (0, 1) acts as per-query learning-rate scaler, which we found sufficient to keep training stable without additional gradient clipping on low-confidence lists. 13 Yuanbao Technical Report

sections.title: C Dataset Details
sections.content: We evaluate on five benchmarks spanning three retrieval paradigms. Table 10 provides an overview, followed by detailed descriptions of each dataset. Table 10: Summary of evaluation datasets. Paradigm Dataset Images Classes Test Split TI II MS COCO Flickr30k 123,287 31,000 5K 1K SoP CUB-200-2011 120,053 11, 22,634 200 60,502 5,924 (T,I)I FashionIQ 77,684 6,016 C.1 Text-to-Image Retrieval (TI) MS COCO (Lin et al., 2014) is large-scale image captioning and retrieval benchmark containing 123,287 images, each annotated with five humanwritten captions. The dataset covers diverse range of everyday scenes with multiple objects and complex spatial relationships. We follow the standard Karpathy split (Karpathy and Fei-Fei, 2015) and report results on the 5K test set, where each text query is matched against all 5K images. Flickr30k (Plummer et al., 2017) consists of 31,000 images collected from the Flickr photosharing platform, each accompanied by five descriptive captions. Compared to MS COCO, Flickr30k features more diverse photographic styles and natural language descriptions with richer linguistic variation. We evaluate on the commonly used 1K test split. C.2 Image-to-Image Retrieval (II) Stanford Online Products (SoP) (Oh Song et al., 2016) is an instance-level product retrieval benchmark containing 120,053 images across 22,634 fine-grained product categories sourced from eBay.com. The dataset is characterized by large intra-class appearance variations (e.g., different viewpoints, lighting conditions, and backgrounds for the same product) and high inter-class similarity among visually related products. The standard split uses 59,551 images from 11,318 categories for training and 60,502 images from 11,316 categories for testing. CUB-200-2011 (Wah et al., 2011) is fine-grained visual recognition dataset consisting of 11,788 bird images from 200 species. The dataset exhibits substantial intra-class variations in pose, viewpoint, and appearance, while inter-class differences can be extremely subtle (e.g., distinguishing between Tencent closely related warbler species). Following the standard evaluation protocol, we use the first 100 species (5,864 images) for training and the remaining 100 species (5,924 images) for testing. C.3 Composed Image Retrieval ((T,I)I) FashionIQ (Wu et al., 2021) is benchmark designed for image retrieval based on natural language feedback in the fashion domain. It contains three categoriesDress, Shirt, and Toptee comprising 77,684 images and 30,134 imagetext image triplets. Each triplet consists of reference image, target image, and two natural language descriptions specifying how the target differs from the reference (e.g., is more colorful and has shorter sleeves). This setup requires models to jointly reason over visual content and textual modification intent. We report results on the standard validation split following prior work (Luo et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2025).

sections.content: D.1 Stage A: Coarse Retrieval We employ different backbone encoders depending on the retrieval paradigm. For text-to-image retrieval on Flickr30k and MS COCO, we use EVA-CLIP-18B (Fang et al., 2023), CLIP-ViTB/32 (Radford et al., 2021), CLIP-ViT-L/14 (Radford et al., 2021), and BLIP-2 (Li et al., 2023). For image-to-image retrieval on SoP and CUB-2002011, we use DINOv2 (Oquab et al., 2024) following the setup of LoCoRE (Xiao et al., 2025). For composed image retrieval on FashionIQ, we use CLIP-ViT-B/32 and CLIP-ViT-L/14. In all settings, we retrieve top-K=20 candidates per query via cosine similarity. The embedding-based matching operator memb in the rubric scoring module reuses the same backbone encoder as Stage A. D.2 Stage B: Teacher Re-ranking We use Gemini-3-flash (Google DeepMind, 2025a) (for EviRank-plus) and Gemini-3-pro (Google DeepMind, 2025b) (for EviRank-pro) as the multimodal teacher models. All structured prompting (caption generation, query expansion, evidence extraction, and listwise ranking) is performed with temperature =0.15 to encourage deterministic outputs. For listwise re-ranking, candidates are processed in batches of 5; when > 8, divideand-merge strategy is applied as described in Appendix A. The rubric scoring hyperparameters in 14 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent Eq. 3 are configured as follows: slot weights ws are set uniformly to 1/S (i.e., 1/6), the forbidden penalty β=0.75, and the consistency weight γ=0.1. D.3 Stage C: Knowledge Distillation We construct the distillation dataset by uniformly sampling 20k queries across all five datasets (4K per dataset: Flickr30k, MS COCO, SoP, CUB-2002011, and FashionIQ). For each sampled query, we execute the full Stage pipeline using Gemini-3pro as the teacher to produce the complete supervision package, including listwise rankings, absolute relevance scores (0100), confidence estimates, hard-pair annotations, and per-slot hit/violation rates. Candidate ordering is randomly shuffled before teacher inference to eliminate position bias. The student model is initialized from Qwen3VL-2B-Thinking (Qwen Team, 2025) and finetuned for 10 epochs using AdamW with cosine learning rate scheduling. sections.title: Bicycle Retrieval
sections.content: G.1.2 Stage 2: Query Expansion Expanded Description: leisure/commuter womens bicycle with classic low step-through curved frame configuration, smooth modern lines, and style balancing sporty aesthetics with everyday practicality. Primary color is bright purple, accented with white brand lettering and minimal black components. Metal frame and fork with smooth glossy paint finish. Fullsize spoked wheel assemblies, stable frame geometry from curved top and down tubes, widened comfort saddle, upright handlebars, and rear single-speed or simple derailleur system. Elongated proportions emphasizing riding stability. Brand logos on frame side, colormatched chain guard and fender areas, functional pedals, chain, braking system, and adjustable seat postsuitable for daily riding and light outdoor use. Figure 4: Case studys bicycle case. This appendix provides comprehensive analysis of EviRanks evidence extraction for the bicycle case study shown in Figure 4. Beyond presenting the extracted evidence, we analyze why each constraint emerges and how it contributes to retrieval accuracy. 16 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent Analysis: The expansion serves two purposes. First, it adds discriminative details that were implicit in the image: elongated proportions, comfort saddle, and upright handlebars collectively define the leisure categorys ergonomic signature. Second, it introduces component-level vocabulary (chain guard, fender, derailleur) that enables precise matching against product descriptions in the gallery. Without this expansion, the retrieval system would rely solely on global visual similarity, missing the fine-grained attributes that distinguish near-identical products. G.2 Evidence Extraction with Dimensional Analysis Global Summary: bicycle displays womens The image leisure/commuter predominantly finished in bright purple, featuring low step-through curved frame with elongated and flowing lines. The configuration emphasizes stability and comfort for daily riding, suitable for urban commuting and light outdoor use. G.2.1 Entities: Category-Level Disambiguation Required: The image features womens leisure/commuter bicycle as the main subject. This product is modern-style city bike with low step-through frame structure and upright riding orientation. Forbidden: The image features mountain bike as the main subject, characterized by robust suspension structure and off-road orientation. This product is road racing bicycle, featuring high top-tube frame and extremely narrow tire configuration. Ignore: The image contains simple and clean presentation environment elements. The frame may contain minor photographic cropping variations. Why These Constraints Emerge: Entity-level evidence targets the most consequential retrieval errorscategory confusion. In embedding space, purple leisure bike may be closer to purple mountain bike than to green leisure bike, because color dominates the learned representation. The required 17 constraints anchor the search to the correct product category, while forbidden constraints explicitly reject the nearest confusable categories. Functional Role: During re-ranking, candidates satisfying entity requirements receive positive scores, while those matching forbidden descriptions receive strong penalties. This creates category gate that filters out high-similarity but wrong-category results before finer attributes are evaluated. G.2.2 Attributes: Visual Property Specification Required: The products primary color is bright purple, complemented by white brand lettering and minimal black components. The frame and fork are constructed from metal material, presenting smooth glossy paint texture. Forbidden: The products primary color is red or orange, complemented by large-area dark camouflage patterns. The frame material is carbon fiber or plastic, presenting matte or rough surface texture. Ignore: Minor shade variations exist within the same purple color family. Normal reflection differences exist on local metal surfaces. Why These Constraints Emerge: Attribute evidence addresses intra-category discrimination. Once the category is established, retrieval must distinguish among dozens of similar leisure bicycles. Color (bright purple vs. red/orange) and material finish (glossy metal vs. matte carbon) are the primary differentiators at this level. Functional Role: The ignore constraints are particularly important here. Without them, lightinginduced color shifts or reflection variations would cause false negativesrejecting correct matches due to superficial differences. By explicitly modeling acceptable variation, EviRank achieves robustness that rigid attribute matching cannot provide. G.2.3 Actions: State and Presentation Mode Required: The bicycle is displayed completely from side view angle, with the body maintaining an upright balanced state. Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent The vehicle is in fully assembled state ready for immediate riding, with all functional components installed. Forbidden: The bicycle is displayed in folded state, with the frame and wheels collapsed together. The vehicle is in disassembled or maintenance state, with multiple key components placed separately. Ignore: Minor forward or backward offset exists in the shooting angle. Small variations exist in wheel orientation during display. Why These Constraints Emerge: Product images of the same bicycle may appear in vastly different statesassembled, partially disassembled, or folded (for folding bikes). The action dimension ensures that presentation state does not confuse identity matching. Functional Role: This dimension prevents subtle failure mode: matching fully assembled leisure bike to component images or maintenance photos of the same product line. The ignore constraints allow matching across minor viewpoint variations that are common in e-commerce photography. G.2.4 Relations: Structural Geometry Verification Required: The front and rear wheels are correctly connected to the frames front fork and rear dropout through spoked wheel assemblies. The handlebars, seat post, and frame form an upright comfortable geometric relationship, emphasizing stable riding posture. Forbidden: The front and rear wheels exhibit obvious misalignment with the frame, with abnormal structural proportions. The handlebars and frame are connected through complex linkage structures, forming an unconventional layout. Ignore: Minor spacing differences exist between components. Local structural alignment variations exist within normal tolerance ranges. Why These Constraints Emerge: Relational evidence captures the geometric signature of product category. Leisure bicycles have characteristic relationship between handlebars, seat, and frame that differs from racing bikes (aggressive forward lean) or mountain bikes (suspension-mediated geometry). Functional Role: This dimension acts as structural consistency check. Even if color and components match, incorrect geometric relationships indicate different product. The forbidden constraints specifically target unconventional designs (recumbent bikes, cargo bikes) that might share individual attributes but differ in overall configuration. G.2.5 Scene: Context Normalization Required: The product is displayed against pure white or light-colored background. The overall scene presents as an e-commerce or product catalog style clean photography environment. Forbidden: The product is displayed in complex outdoor mountain environment. The overall scene presents as cluttered indoor space containing numerous other objects. Ignore: Minor brightness variations exist in the background. Subtle shadow differences exist in ambient lighting. Why These Constraints Emerge: Scene evidence explicitly models the presentation context, which is major source of embedding noise. The same bicycle photographed in studio versus on mountain trail produces dramatically different embeddings, despite identical product identity. Functional Role: By requiring studio-style presentation and ignoring minor background variations, this dimension normalizes context-induced similarity distortions. The forbidden constraints prevent matching to lifestyle photography where the product may be partially occluded or shown at unusual angles. G.2.6 Key Details: Discriminative Feature Anchoring Required: Brand logos are clearly printed on the frame side as an important identifying feature. The bicycle is equipped with color-matched chain guard and widened comfort saddle, reflecting daily riding orientation. 18 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent Forbidden: Required: Positive evidence that must be Exaggerated racing numbers and competitive presentdefines what the target is. sponsor logos are printed on the frame. The vehicle is equipped with dual-crown suspension forks and large-diameter disc brake systems as core features. Ignore: Minor differences exist in brand font sizing. Slight positional variations exist in non-critical decals. Why These Constraints Emerge: Key details capture the most discriminative local featureselements that uniquely identify specific product or product line. Brand logos and signature components (color-matched chain guard) serve as visual fingerprints. Functional Role: This dimension handles the final disambiguation when multiple candidates pass all other checks. The forbidden constraints are particularly valuable: racing numbers and professional-grade suspension are strong negative indicators that immediately disqualify competitive cycling products, even if they share color and basic frame geometry. G.3 Integrated Analysis: How Evidence Dimensions Interact The six dimensions form hierarchical filtering system: 1. Entities establishes category boundaries, eliminating cross-category confusion (mountain bikes, road bikes). 2. Attributes performs intra-category discrimination based on visual properties (color, material, finish). 3. Actions filters presentation state mismatches (assembled vs. disassembled). 4. Relations verifies structural consistency with expected geometric configurations. 5. Scene normalizes context variations that affect embedding similarity. 6. Key Details anchors to unique identifying features for final disambiguation. The three-way (required/forbidden/ignore) operates consistently across all dimensions: constraint structure Forbidden: Negative evidence that must be absentdefines what the target is not. Ignore: Variation tolerancedefines what does not matter for identity. This structured approach transforms retrieval from opaque similarity scoring into transparent logical evaluation, where each dimensions contribution can be independently assessed and explained.

sections.title: H Prompt Templates
sections.content: This appendix presents the complete prompt templates used across the EviRank pipeline. We employ four logical prompt modules: P-CAP for initial caption generation (Section H.1), P-B0 for query understanding and expansion (Section H.2), P-B1 for structured evidence slot mining (Section H.3), and P-RANK for listwise re-ranking inference (Section H.4). The four modules are documented separately for clarity, but at inference time they are merged into two online calls: P-CAP/PB0/P-B1 are completed within single structured evidence-extraction request, and P-RANK issues one listwise call over the rubric top-M candidates (Section 4.1). All prompts are invoked in training-free manner with no task-specific fine-tuning. Placeholders enclosed in braces (e.g., {query}) are filled at runtime with actual queryspecific content. H.1 Prompt P-Cap: Caption Generation Prompt P-CAP (Figure 5) serves as the entry point of the evidence extraction pipeline. It converts raw product image into rich, multi-aspect textual description covering five complementary dimensions: overall appearance, color and material, structural details, design features, and functional elements. This five-way decomposition is intentionally designed to mirror the evidence-slot taxonomy introduced in Section 3.1, ensuring that the generated caption already contains the fine-grained information needed for downstream evidence mining. The prompt is particularly critical for image-toimage retrieval where no user-provided text exists, as the caption becomes the sole textual anchor for all subsequent stages. By requesting 35 detailed sentences, we ensure sufficient specificity for discriminating among visually similar products while 19 Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent PROMPT P-CAP Detailed Caption Generation You are an expert at generating comprehensive and detailed visual descriptions for product images. Your task is to create thorough description that captures both the overall appearance and fine-grained details of the product. Query Image: <attached> Generate detailed product description that includes: 1. Overall Appearance Product type/category; general shape and form factor; overall style (modern, vintage, classic, sporty, etc.). 2. Color & Material Primary colors and any color patterns/combinations; material composition (metal, plastic, leather, fabric, wood, etc.); surface texture and finish (matte, glossy, brushed, etc.). 3. Structural Details Key components and parts; construction and assembly details; size proportions and dimensions (relative terms). 4. Design Features Unique design elements or patterns; branding, logos, or text if present; decorative elements or embellishments. 5. Functional Elements Visible functional parts; hardware, fasteners, or connectors; any moving parts or adjustable features. Please provide comprehensive description in 35 detailed sentences that would allow someone to accurately identify and distinguish this specific product from similar items. Be as specific and descriptive as possible about visual characteristics. Output: Only the detailed description text, nothing else. Figure 5: Prompt P-CAP for detailed caption generation. keeping the output concise enough for efficient processing. H.3 Prompt P-B1: Structured Evidence Slot Mining H.2 Prompt P-B0: Query Understanding & Expansion Prompt P-B0 (Figure 6) enriches the raw caption from the previous stage with background knowledge and semantic context (Section 3.2). The output contains three key fields. expanded_query augments the original description with concrete visual details that are implicit in the caption such as typical use scenarios and related product conceptsthereby improving recall for semantically relevant but lexically dissimilar candidates. core_intent distils the single most discriminative identity statement, serving as the primary semantic anchor during evidence-slot extraction. confidence is self-assessed reliability estimate of the expansion itself; it is used only to monitor and, if necessary, discard degenerate expansions, and should not be confused with the listwise confidence that weights the distillation loss in Stage (Eq. 4), which is produced by P-RANK. The prompt is conditioned on the caption alone: image paths, filenames and directory names are never exposed to the teacher at any stage, so no category prior can leak from the dataset layout into the evidence package. 20 Prompt P-B1 (Figure 7) is the core evidencemining prompt. It decomposes the enriched query into six orthogonal semantic dimensions ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTES, ACTIONS, RELATIONS, SCENE, and KEYDETAILSeach further organized into required, forbidden, and ignore constraint lists. Two design choices are notewor- (i) Affirmative-only wording. All conthy. straint sentences, including those in the forbidden list, are phrased as positive statements that describe what wrong match looks like rather than negating the target. For instance, instead of The bicycle should not be red, the forbidden constraint states The bicycle is red with black handlebars. This ensures that every constraint can be directly compared with candidate descriptions via embedding cosine similarity (Eqs. 23), yielding stable and sign-consistent matching scores. (ii) Explicit scoring guidance. The prompt communicates the intended scoring logic (score = (cid:80) required_match (cid:80) forbidden_match), aligning constraint generation with the downstream deterministic rubric (Eq. 3) and reducing misalignment between extraction and evaluation. H.4 Prompt P-Rank: Listwise Re-ranking During inference, the teacher MLLM receives both the query image and all top-K candidate images simultaneously, together with the structured evidence Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent PROMPT P-B0 Query Understanding & Expansion You are query understanding and expansion expert. Given detailed image caption/description, you need to: (1) Understand the core visual characteristics and product identity; (2) Provide contextual background and semantic expansion; (3) Output in structured JSON format. Input Caption: query Please analyze and output in the following JSON format: { "original_query": "expanded_query": related concepts, and image-specific considerations>", "core_intent": and distinguishing features>", "confidence": } 0. "<original caption/query>", "<expanded description with background context, "<one sentence describing the main visual identity Requirements: expanded_query should add relevant visual and semantic context while preserving all original details. core_intent should capture the most distinctive visual characteristics. confidence should be number between 0.0 and 1.0. Rely only on the caption; do not use filenames, directory names, or any other dataset-side metadata. Output ONLY the JSON object, no additional text before or after. Ensure all strings are properly escaped. Figure 6: Prompt P-B0 for query understanding and expansion. text distilled from the preceding stages. The evidence text presented to the re-ranker is assembled at runtime from the outputs of P-B0 and P-B1 following compact serialization format (described after the prompt box). Figure 8 presents the full re-ranking prompt. The re-ranking prompt is designed around three (i) Evidence-conditioned ranking. principles. The evidence constraints ({evidence_text}) are placed prominently before the candidate list, ensuring that the teacher attends to structured required/forbidden constraints as the primary decision basis rather than relying solely on holistic visual impression. This directly implements the rubric-first stabilization strategy. (ii) Multimodal listwise input. Both the query image and all candidate images are presented in single prompt turn, enabling the teacher to perform direct visual comparison across candidates rather than scoring each independently. The images are base64-encoded with controlled resolution (max_edge=2048) and JPEG quality (quality=85) to balance vi- (iii) Strucsual fidelity and token efficiency. tured JSON output. By requiring strict JSON schema with permutation of candidate indices, we eliminate ambiguity in parsing and guarantee valid ranking. The same call also returns the three supervision fields consumed by Stage C: relevance_scores provide the teacher scores used in Lscore, confidence provides the weight in Eq. 4, and hard_pairs provides for Lpair; only ranked_indices is needed to produce the final ranking at test time. The accompanying brief_reasoning field, while not used in the final score, provides interpretable rationales that are valuable for error analysis. We anonymize candidate identifiers (replacing filenames with opaque indices) before presenting them to the teacher, so that no dataset-side metadata reaches the re-ranker. For large candidate sets (K > 8), we adopt divide-and-merge batching strategy: candidates are partitioned into groups of size (default B=5), each group is independently ranked by the teacher, and the resulting sub-lists are iteratively merged via pairwise re-ranking calls. With = K/B groups this costs 2n 1 calls in total and 1 + log2 sequential rounds when merges at the same tree level are issued in parallel, which keeps inference cost tractable while preserving global ranking quality. H.5 Evidence Text Assembly The {evidence_text} placeholder in PRANK is populated at runtime by serializing the outputs of P-B0 and P-B1 into compact textual format. Figure 9 shows the assembly template. As shown in Figure 9, the assembled evidence text follows three-tier hierarchy: query-level summaries (core intent, expanded query, global summary), followed by slot-level constraint blocks. Within each slot, required and forbidden constraint sentences are serialized as pipe-delimited strings, Yuanbao Technical Report Tencent PROMPT P-B1 Structured Evidence Slot Mining You are visual evidence extraction expert for image-to-image retrieval. Given detailed image caption, extract structured evidence that would help identify matching images. Input Caption: query Your task is to extract evidence into 6 semantic slots, with each slot containing 24 complete affirmative sentences (not phrases). Organize into Required / Forbidden / Ignore lists: Required: Affirmative sentences describing visual elements that MUST be present for correct match. Example: The bicycle is blue with silver handlebars. Forbidden: Affirmative sentences describing visual elements that would indicate WRONG match. These describe what incorrect matches would look like. Example: The bicycle is red with black handlebars. Ignore: Affirmative sentences describing similar but non-critical visual elements that can be tolerated. Scoring logic: score = (cid:80) (required_match_scores) (cid:80) (forbidden_match_scores) Output in the following JSON format: { "global_summary": "entities": "attributes": "actions": "relations": "scene": "key_details": {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]} } {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]}, {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]}, {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]}, {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]}, {"required":[...], "forbidden":[...], "ignore":[...]}, "<2-3 sentences providing an overall visual summary>", Requirements: All sentences must be affirmative (positive statements), including forbidden items. Forbidden sentences describe what wrong matches look like (positive form), NOT using not or should not. Each entry should be complete sentence; each list should have 24 sentences. Base the evidence strictly on the visual content described in the caption; do not rely on filenames, directories, or any external metadata. Sentences should be specific and descriptive for accurate embedding matching. Output ONLY valid JSON, no markdown code blocks, no explanations. Figure 7: Prompt P-B1 for structured evidence slot mining. with maximum of six sentences per list to control prompt length. Notably, the ignore constraints are deliberately excluded from the re-ranking prompt. This is because their role is to calibrate the deterministic rubric scoring (Eq. 3) by masking nondiscriminative variations, whereas the MLLM reranker is expected to internalize such tolerance through its own visual reasoning. Including ignore constraints would increase prompt length without providing actionable ranking guidance. This selective serialization keeps the evidence text compact (typically 200400 tokens) while preserving all decision-critical information. Together, the four prompts form progressive refinement pipeline: P-CAP grounds the image in language, P-B0 enriches the description with semantic context, P-B1 structures the enriched representation into checkable constraints, and P-RANK leverages the full evidence package for listwise visual re-ranking. Each stage builds upon the previous ones output, creating coherent chain from raw pixels to interpretable, evidence-conditioned ranking decisions.

sections.title: N Detailed Comparison with ImageScope
sections.content: ImageScope (Luo et al., 2025) is the most closely related multi-stage MLLM-based re-ranker, and it likewise unifies heterogeneous queries before invoking an MLLM. We therefore make the formulation-level differences explicit. Different unification targets. ImageScope unifies queries into single natural-language description of the users intent and lets the MLLM perform holistic reasoning over that description. The unified representation is therefore still piece of free-form text, and the relevance decision is recovered implicitly from the MLLMs reasoning trace. EviRank, in contrast, unifies queries into typed evidence package E(q) consisting of slot-wise required/forbidden/ignorable constraints. The unified representation is itself an evaluation rubric, and relevance is recovered explicitly via constraint verification rather than holistic reasoning. failure surfaces. Because Different ImageScopes representation is holistic description followed by free-form reasoning, it inherits the three failure modes of CoT-based re-rankers discussed in Section 2 (omission of unstated constraints, hallucinated evidence, and inconsistent semantic coverage across queries). EviRanks typed-evidence representation directly addresses these failure modes: required and forbidden statements force the model to commit to which dimensions matter before comparing candidates; ignorable statements explicitly model what should not be penalized; and the slot schema is fixed across queries, making coverage uniform and auditable. Auditability and supervision. Holistic descriptions are not decomposable: it is hard to ask which part of the description is satisfied by candidate c? or to extract per-dimension supervision signals from single free-form passage. EviRanks evidence package is decomposable by construction, which (i) yields per-slot satisfaction and violation rates that can be inspected and verified independently, and (ii) provides structured supervision (slot-wise indicators, hard pairs, calibrated scores) that can be distilled into smaller student neither of which is naturally available from holisticdescription pipelines.
